key_insight: GPT-5 achieved substantial or almost perfect agreement with radiologist labels for 7 of 9 incidental findings, but no model–prompt combination performed best across all findings.
clinical_relevance: Automated labeling could support research and quality-review workflows for incidental findings documented in lung cancer screening CT reports.
method: Retrospective analysis of 300 CT reports from one Dutch academic hospital, dated 2003–2020.
Compared four LLMs using four prompting strategies each, plus keyword-based search.
Evaluated against radiologist labels using Cohen’s kappa, sensitivity, specificity, and F1.
evidence_signal: GPT-5’s kappa ranged from 0.71–0.97 for seven findings; the best reported agreement for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass was moderate (0.48 and 0.42, respectively).
watch_item: Single-center, report-level evaluation does not establish generalizability or accuracy for detecting findings directly on CT images.
paper_title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
